sanskrit: ye 'śraddhayā dhanakāmyāt kravyādā samāsate | te vā anyeṣāṃ kumbhīṃ pary ādadhati sarvadā ||
english: Those flesh-eaters who gather together without faith, out of greed for wealth — they always snatch away the water-pot of others.

sanskrit: iṣīkāṃ caratīṃ vittvā tilpiyaṃ daṇḍanaṃ naḍam | tān indra idhmaṃ kṛtvā yamasyāgniṃ nirādadhau ||
english: Knowing the iṣīkā-reed that wanders, the tilpiya-plant, the staff-plant, the reed — Indra, making them into fuel, consigned them into Yama's fire.

sanskrit: aviḥ kṛṣṇā bhāgadheyaṃ paśūnāṃ sīsaṃ kravyād uta candraṃ ta āhuḥ | māṣāḥ piṣṭā bhāgadheyaṃ havyaṃ te 'raṇyānyā gahvaraṃ sacasva ||
english: The black ewe is the appointed share among cattle; lead, they say, is the flesh-eater's — and the moon as well. Ground black lentils are the oblation, their fitting share. Go thou into the thicket of the wild forest.

sanskrit: pratyañcam arkaṃ pratyarpayitvā pravidvān panthāṃ vi hy ācakāra | parāmīṣām asūn dideśa dīrgheṇāyuṣā sam adhād ihemān ||
english: Having directed back the sun toward the west, the knowing one indeed opened up the path. He pointed away the life-breaths of those others and, with long life, established these ones here.

sanskrit: anaḍvāhaṃ plavam anv ārabhadhvaṃ sa vo nirvakṣad duritād avadyāt | ā rohata savitur nāvaṃ hiraṇyayīṃ ṣaḍbhir ūrmibhir amatiṃ carema ||
english: Take hold of the bull as your raft — he shall carry you out of misfortune, out of disgrace. Mount the golden ship of Savitṛ; with six waves may we pass beyond darkness.

sanskrit: gobhiṣ ṭaremāmatiṃ durevāṃ yavena kṣudhaṃ puruhūta viśvām | vayaṃ rājānaḥ prathamā dhanānām ariṣṭāsa ṛjanībhis tarema ||
english: With cattle may we cross the hard-going darkness; with barley, O much-invoked Indra, all hunger. We, kings, foremost claimants of wealth, unharmed, may we cross over with straight paths.

sanskrit: pūrṇaṃ nāri pra harābhi kumbham apāṃ rasair oṣadhīnāṃ ghṛtasya | imān pātṝṃr amṛtenā sam aṅdhi sthirā vīrāḥ saṃmanaso bhavantu ||
english: O woman, bring forward the full jar, filled with the essences of waters, of plants, of ghee. Anoint these drinkers with the immortal nectar; may they be steadfast heroes, of united mind.

sanskrit: pumān puṃso adhi tiṣṭha carma tatra hvayasva yatamā priyā te | yāvantāv agre prathamaṃ sameyathus tad vāṃ vayo yamarājye samānam ||
english: O man, stand upon the hide of the man; summon there whichever woman is dear to you. As great as you two were when you first came together in the beginning — that same youth of yours is united in the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: tāvad vāṃ tejas tati vīryāṇi tāvac cakṣus tatidhā vājināni | agniḥ śarīraṃ sacate yadaidho adhā pakvān mithunā saṃ bhavāthaḥ ||
english: As great is the radiance spread out between you two, as great the vigor spread in the same measure, as great the eye spreading abundantly with strength — fire accompanies the body when it blazes; then, when ripened, you two as a couple shall come together.

sanskrit: sam asmiṃl loke sam u devayāne saṃ smā sametaṃ yamarājye | pūtau pavitrair upa tad u hvayethāṃ yadyad reto adhi vāṃ saṃbabhūva ||
english: Come together in this world, come together also on the path of the gods; you have always come together in the kingdom of Yama. Purified by purifying rites, call each other toward that — whatever seed has been born between the two of you.

sanskrit: āpaḥ putrāso abhi saṃ viśadhvam imaṃ jīvaṃ jīvadhanyāḥ sam eta | tāsāṃ bhajadhvam amṛtaṃ yad āhur yam odanaṃ pacati vo janitrī ||
english: O sons who are the waters, enter into this living one; you who hold life, come together. Share among yourselves the immortality which they speak of — that rice-porridge which your mother cooks for you.

sanskrit: yaṃ vaḥ pitā pacati yaṃ ca mātā riprān nirmukthyai śamalāc ca vācaḥ | sa odanaḥ śatadhāraḥ svarga ubhe vyāpa nabhasī mahitvā ||
english: That which your father cooks and that which your mother cooks — for release from defilement and from the taint of speech — that rice-porridge, having a hundred streams, heavenly, by its greatness pervades both the two expanses of the sky.

sanskrit: ubhe nabhasī ubhayāṃś ca lokān ye yajvanām abhijitāḥ svargāḥ | teṣāṃ jyotiṣmān madhumān yo agre tasmin putrair jarasi saṃ śrayethām ||
english: Both expanses of the sky and both worlds — those heavenly regions won by sacrificers — the one among them that is luminous and sweet, that is foremost: upon that one may you two, with your sons, take refuge in old age.

sanskrit: prācīṃprācīṃ pradiśam ā rabhetām etaṃ lokaṃ śraddadhānāḥ sacante | mimāthāṃ pātraṃ tad vāṃ pūrṇam astu sa vāṃ pakvaḥ pitryāṇe nyāyat ||
english: Let the two of them take hold of every eastern direction; those who have faith follow this world. You two have measured the vessel — may it be full for you. That cooked offering, ripened, shall flow down to you two in the realm of the fathers.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāṃ diśam abhi nakṣamāṇau pary āvartethām abhi pātram etat | tasmai vāṃ yamaḥ pitṛbhiḥ saṃvidānaḥ pakvāya śarma bahulaṃ ni yacchāt ||
english: Turning toward the southern direction, moving swiftly, let the two of them circle around this vessel. For the sake of that — the cooked offering — may Yama, in agreement with the fathers, grant you two abundant shelter.

sanskrit: pratīcī diśām iyam id varaṃ vāṃ yasyāṃ somo adhipā mṛḍitā ca | tasyāṃ mimāthāṃ sukṛtaḥ sacethām adhā pakvena saha saṃ bhavema ||
english: The western direction — this indeed is the better one for you two, in which Soma is the overlord and the gracious. In that direction you two have measured; may the righteous accompany you. Then may we come together along with the cooked offering.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ rāṣṭraṃ prajayottarāvad diśām udīcī kṛṇavan no agram | pāṅktaṃ chandaḥ puruṣo babhūva viśvair viśvāṅgaiḥ saha saṃ bhavema ||
english: The northern realm, enriched with progeny, making the north direction our foremost — the pankti meter became the person. May we come together with all, with all his limbs.

sanskrit: dhruveyaṃ virāṇ namo astv asyai śivā putrebhya uta mahyam astu | sā no devy adite viśvavāra irya iva gopā abhi rakṣa pakvam ||
english: This Virāj is steadfast — let homage be to her; may she be auspicious to our sons and to me. O goddess Aditi, all-desirable, guard our cooked offering as a cowherd guards his cattle.

sanskrit: piteva putrām̐ abhi saṃ sacasva naḥ śivā no vātā iha vāntu śagmāḥ | yam odanaṃ pacato devate iha taṃ nas tapa uta satyaṃ ma vittām ||
english: Like a father, accompany us together with our sons; may the winds blow here upon us auspiciously, bringing ease. O two divinities, who cook the rice-porridge here — heat it for us and know it truly as ours.

sanskrit: yadyat kṛṣṇaḥ śakuna eha gatvā tsaraṃ viṣaktaṃ bila āsasāda | dāsī vā yad ārdrahastā samaṅkta ulūkhalaṃ musalaṃ śundhatāpaḥ ||
english: Whatever black bird, flying here, came upon the mortar lodged and stuck in the hollow — or whatever slave-woman, with wet hand, smeared the mortar and pestle: purify them, burn them clean.

sanskrit: ayaṃ grāvā pṛthubudhno vayodhāḥ pūtaḥ pavitrair apa hantu rakṣaḥ | ā roha carma mahi śarma yaccha mā dampatī pautram aghaṃ ni gātām ||
english: This pressing-stone, broad-based, bearer of strength — purified by purifying rites, let it drive away the demon. Mount the hide, bestow great shelter; let not the master and mistress of the house descend into the sin that harms their grandson.

sanskrit: vanaspatiḥ saha devair na āgan rakṣaḥ piśācām̐ apabādhamānaḥ | sa ucchrayātai pra vadāti vācaṃ tena lokām̐ abhi sarvāñ jayema ||
english: The lord of the forest has come to us together with the gods, driving away demons and flesh-eating spirits. Let him be raised up high, let him speak forth his voice; by him may we conquer all the worlds.

sanskrit: sapta medhāṃ paśavaḥ pary agṛhṇan ya eṣāṃ medasvān uta yaś cakarśa | trayastriṃśad devatās tvāṃ sacante sa naḥ svargam abhi neṣi lokam ||
english: Seven animal offerings received the sacrificial fat — the one among them that was rich in fat and the one that was lean. Thirty-three divinities accompany you; lead us toward the heavenly world.

sanskrit: svargaṃ lokam abhi no nayāsi saṃ jāyā saha putraiḥ syāma | gṛhṇāmi hastam anv aitv atra mā nas tārīn nirṛtir mo arātiḥ ||
english: Lead us toward the heavenly world; may we be united — wife together with sons. I take hold of the hand; let her follow here. May Nirṛti not pass us by, nor enmity.

sanskrit: grāhiṃ pāpmānam ati tām̐ ayāma tamo vyasya pra vadāsi valgu ||  vānaspatya udyato mā jihiṃsīr mā taṇḍulaṃ vi śarīr devayantam ||
english: Past that evil seizure may we go; dispelling darkness, speak thou sweetly. O implement born of the forest, raised up, do not injure us; do not shatter the grain that is going to the gods.

sanskrit: viśvavyacā ghṛtapṛṣṭho bhaviṣyaṃ sayonir lokam upa yāhi vidvān | varṣavṛddham upa yaccha śūrpe tviṣiṃ palāvān apa tad vinaktu ||
english: O wide-spreading one, ghee-backed, destined to be — knowing, of one womb, go toward that world. Present in the winnowing basket what has grown with rain; let it winnow away the chaff, removing that lustre from the husks.

sanskrit: trayo lokāḥ saṃmitā brāhmaṇena dyaur evāsau pṛthivy antarikṣam | aṃśūn gṛbhitān anu saṃrabhethām ā pyāyantāṃ punar ā yantu śūrpāt ||
english: Three worlds are measured by the brahman: yonder sky, earth, and the atmosphere between. Let the two of them take hold of the stalks that have been grasped; may they swell and come back again from the winnowing basket.
